Bethnal Green to Mile End | 83

claims.text: TfL in-cab measurements taken on 24 June 2024 recorded 82 dB LAeq westbound from Mile End to Bethnal Green and 86 dB LAeq from Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street.

citations.quote: Mile End to Bethnal Green | 82
Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street | 86

claims.text: In TfL's 24 June 2024 in-cab data, eastbound sound levels between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green were 4 dB higher than between Bethnal Green and Mile End.
Our uncalibrated relative phone audio measurements recorded -18.66 dBFS(A) eastbound from Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and -19.42 dBFS(A) eastbound from Bethnal Green to Mile End.
Our uncalibrated relative phone audio measurements recorded -18.8 dBFS(A) westbound from Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street and -19.07 dBFS(A) westbound from Mile End to Bethnal Green.
Our uncalibrated relative measurements across eleven runs found a mean within-trip contrast of 0.54 dB between Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and Bethnal Green to Mile End.
Indicative sound level meter app readings over one whole trip including platform and dwell time recorded 91.9 dB(A) LAeq eastbound between Liverpool Street and Mile End and 87.3 dB(A) LAeq westbound.
A secondary press report citing JRPass attributed an average noise level of 92.8 decibels to the Central line between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels
Daniel de Nieuwe, Head of Product from JRPass said:

claims.text: Our uncalibrated relative phone measurements and indicative app readings cannot be compared directly with TfL in-cab figures or secondary media reports.
Public records do not confirm which track direction was treated during earlier grinding, whether grinding was repeated after 2022, or whether the 2023/24 deep Tube reconditioning was completed.
During Mayor's Question Time 2026/2156, Elly Baker AM stated that TfL Government Relations responded to her request by turning down the majority of the requests for data.

citations.quote: turning down the majority of the requests for data.

asks.request: Request the complete log of rail grinding interventions carried out on the Central line between Liverpool Street and Mile End from June 2022 to date, specifying track direction, dates, and whether work was for safety defects or noise mitigation.
asks.why: Resolves the evidentiary gap identified in claim_limits_history regarding whether grinding has recurred since the December 2021 to May 2022 works cited in claim_grinding_completed_2022.

asks.request: Request the status and verification reports for the deep Tube reconditioning planned for financial year 2023/24 on the Central line eastbound between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green.
asks.why: Establishes whether long-term track replacement occurred as scheduled in claim_reconditioning_planned_2023_2024 or remains outstanding.

asks.request: Request TfL's bi-monthly in-cab noise monitoring records for the Central line from July 2024 through 2026, alongside any passenger saloon noise surveys conducted on the section.
asks.why: Updates the single 24 June 2024 snapshot from claim_tfl_cab_eb_2024 and claim_tfl_cab_wb_2024 and bridges cab versus saloon acoustic conditions.

asks.request: Request the primary dataset and calculation methodology underpinning the 92.8 dB figure reported for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green.
asks.why: Clarifies whether the media figure cited in claim_secondary_press_figure originated from official TfL data or external uncalibrated measurements.

reasons: numbers not supported by the cited quotes/stats/formula: ['2022', '2023', '24']
